mechanism_summary: The ResourceQuota checkout-quota in the checkout namespace caps pods at 2, so quota admission rejects every pod create beyond that cap with 'exceeded quota'; the checkout-api ReplicaSet therefore cannot create its remaining pods and the deployment stays well below its intended 6 replicas.
decisive_evidence: ReplicaSet FailedCreate events in namespace checkout with message 'Error creating: pods ... is forbidden: exceeded quota: checkout-quota' (kubectl get events -n checkout / describe rs), corroborated by resourcequota/checkout-quota showing hard pods: 2 against the deployment's spec.replicas: 6.
remediation_summary: Raise the pods cap on the checkout/checkout-quota ResourceQuota to cover the intended scale — kubectl patch resourcequota checkout-quota -n checkout --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"hard":{"pods":"8"}}}' — or delete the quota (kubectl delete resourcequota checkout-quota -n checkout); the ReplicaSet controller then creates the remaining pods with no deployment change.
